points.description: Chooses a paint color (any of the four) and gives a description consistent with that choice: states how the color would affect the inside of the doghouse (e.g., light gray/white would keep the inside cooler; black/dark gray would make it warmer). Equivalent wording accepted.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if a color is chosen but the effect on the inside temperature is missing, vague, or inconsistent with the choice.

points.description: Supports the choice with specific experimental data, e.g., white lid had the lowest average air temperature (42°C) versus black (53°C), or light gray 45°C, dark gray 48°C; the lighter the lid, the lower the temperature. The data must match the chosen color.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the data are referenced only generally (e.g., 'lighter colors were cooler') without specific values, or if a value is given but not linked to the choice.

rubric.notes: Full marks: a chosen color, a consistent explanation of its effect on the doghouse interior, and specific data from the table supporting it. Part marks for a choice with an effect but no data, or general data without numbers. Any color can earn marks if reasoned consistently with the data (e.g., white or light gray for a hot climate keeps the dog cooler).
